description: The company's own WhatsApp number, linked as a device through a small whatsmeow bridge in the same container: every chat is a Bandeja ticket, the agent answers what is its to answer the moment it arrives, and steps aside while the owner answers from her phone
client_copy: Contesta los mensajes de tu WhatsApp que puede contestar solo, te deja en la Bandeja los que tenés que ver vos, y si contestás vos desde tu teléfono, no se mete.
_comment: THE NUMBER LIVES IN A SECOND PROCESS, NOT HERE. `engine/whatsapp-bridge/`
is a small Go program over whatsmeow, built into the engine's image and
started by the entrypoint ONLY when this plugin is in CORE_PLUGINS. It
listens on loopback, keeps whatsmeow's store on the state volume
/internal/whatsapp/events, which pokes the flow so a reply is seconds away.
LINKED AS A DEVICE, NOT THE BUSINESS API: the owner scans a QR from the
portal with her own WhatsApp, like WhatsApp Web. That is why the bridge is
careful: it never enumerates contacts or pictures, it only answers inbound,
one send at a time, and a `rate-overlimit` pauses that kind of call for
thirty minutes instead of retrying through it.
ANSWERS GO OUT WITHOUT THE CLIENT'S YES (Luis, 24/9/2026, for every
channel), and what is not the agent's to answer is decided by
`skills/whatsapp` and goes to the board instead. When the OWNER answers a
chat from her phone, that chat is hers for WHATSAPP_TAKEOVER_MINUTES (120)
and the code will not send into it.
IT REQUIRES `kanban`: each chat is one Bandeja ticket, source=whatsapp and
the chat's phone JID as source_ref, opened and written by code.
